column1: # Game profile of Raging Loop (Switch, base game 1.0.0 = v0). Plays on the Mac
# Unity 2018.3.10f1 (IL2CPP) with FMOD, SDK 7.3.2 (its sdk and subsdk0 are DRAGON QUEST XI S's builds); subsdk0 is the movie module, which plays the opening movie, an MP4 of H.264 and AAC.
# No bundles: the 48 shaders are Unity's Shader objects in Data/*.assets and Data/Resources, whose serialized files carry no type trees, so unityfs.py has Unity 2018.3's Shader layout
# written out (KNOWN_TREES); the story's pictures are loose PNG / JPG files in StreamingAssets that the game loads itself.
# Controller only (the game reads no touch, docked or handheld): it stays docked (1920x1080) with the 2D pad layout; the left stick moves the menu cursor

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true: nninitStartup hands application pool − used memory to StandardAllocator as virtual address memory,

# one address region in the alias region, and the game never calls SetMemoryHeapSize. The cuts for this sdk build (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py, DRAGON QUEST XI S's) put that region 64 MB into the alias region
# (node area 62 MB, regions of 1 GB and more 32 MB aligned). Unlike Unity 2020 and 2022 (Ace Attorney Investigations Collection, Monster Train 2: a 1 GB pool), Unity 2018.3 reserves no
# address regions of its own: every page the game maps lies in StandardAllocator's region (Mac, DM_SVC map log over the title, the tutorial and the opening: 377 MB mapped at the peak),
# so the hardware pool (3.2 GB, StandardAllocator to +3.21 GB of the 4.375 GB alias region) leaves no address space short, and only mapped pages cost memory.
# Engage's 5 GB block: 256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; Unity Shader objects, read by unityfs.py) ----
# The registered build selects near-zero NVN depth; offline pipeline bases use main0_z.
